A B-cell depleting agent has been given to a few dozen patients with immune
thrombocytopenia in a dose escalation and a single expansion cohort, with
serial drug concentrations, B-cell counts and platelet counts. Can a model of
those three time courses select the Phase 2 dose? The literature has the
platelet half of that model and the B-cell half, in separate places and for
separate drugs, and nothing that joins them in this disease. The references
document widens the search to every ITP drug that blocks antibody-mediated
platelet destruction, and asks why the join is missing. Nothing has been fit
here yet.

## Documents

- [Working specification](specification.qmd). Section 2 gives the ITP endpoint
  definitions from the IWG 2009 consensus paper. Then the model, the data it
  requires, the identifiability problems, the dose selection rule, and the
  simulation study that scores the rule against picking the highest safe dose.
  Section 19 gives the reasons no such model has been published, split into
  those that apply here and those that do not, with a table of every attempt. Its
  **In brief** section is one screen and says what the rest argues.
- [References](references.qmd). The literature review that opens with what
  exists and what does not, then the reading queue in order, then a marker on
  every source recording whether the specification's use of it has been
  checked, plus the FDA, EMA and PMDA reviews of the three ITP drugs that
  block platelet destruction, read in full, and a table of the TPO-RA
  PK-platelet models the specification borrows from. Six sources have been
  read; the rest are ❌.
